analysis_summary: Comprehensive analysis of NLM codebase reveals a mature Phase 2 implementation with strong foundations but significant integration gaps. The core neural computation (spiking neurons, STDP, Hebbian plasticity, structural plasticity) is well-implemented and tested, but memory systems, prediction systems, and configuration management need completion and integration.

issues: ConfigValue variant includes many types but no type conversion utilities
ConfigEntry struct defined but not fully used
No JSON support for configuration files
suggested_fixes: Implement loadFromArgs() with command line parsing
Add validation and type safety for configuration values
files_to_improve.implementation_approach: Implement configuration file loading, command line parsing, and type-safe value access

issues: Memory systems declared in Brain.hpp but not initialized in Brain.cpp
Forward-declared cognitive systems not implemented (NeuralPlanner, ConceptFormation, AttentionalSelection)
Forward-declared neuromodulatory systems not implemented (Dopamine, Curiosity, Novelty, PredictionError)
Tight coupling between Brain and all subsystems
suggested_fixes: Implement Brain.cpp with proper initialization of all memory systems
Implement missing cognitive systems (NeuralPlanner, ConceptFormation, AttentionalSelection)
Implement missing neuromodulatory systems (Dopamine, Curiosity, Novelty, PredictionError)
Refactor Brain class to use composition over inheritance for better modularity
files_to_improve.implementation_approach: Implement Brain.cpp with comprehensive system integration, implement all forward-declared cognitive and neuromodulatory systems, refactor Brain class architecture

issues: PlasticityRule base class has placeholder implementations for AntiHebbianRule, BCMRule, and HebbianRule
Base PlasticityRule methods (isEnabled, setEnabled) have no implementations
Two plasticity rule systems exist: main one in src/plasticity/ and this one in PlasticityRule.hpp
suggested_fixes: Implement missing PlasticityRule base class methods
Consider consolidating into a single plasticity rule architecture
files_to_improve.implementation_approach: Implement missing base class methods, implement missing plasticity rules, consider architecture consolidation

issues.title: Dual Architecture Systems
issues.description: Two separate plasticity rule architectures exist, causing confusion and duplication
examples: Main plasticity system: src/plasticity/ (STDP, Hebbian, StructuralPlasticity)
Alternative system: PlasticityRule.hpp (AntiHebbianRule, BCMRule)
Brain.hpp includes both STDP and Hebbian from src/plasticity/

issues.title: Interface Surface Area
issues.description: Brain class has excessive interface methods (183 public methods)
examples: Brain manages neural regions, spike systems, plasticity, memory, prediction, cognition, neuromodulation
Single class violates Single Responsibility Principle
Tight coupling makes testing and maintenance difficult

issues.title: Incomplete Integration
issues.description: Memory and prediction systems exist but are not integrated with Brain
examples: Brain.hpp declares memory system getters but Brain.cpp doesn't initialize them
Prediction systems have implementations but Brain.cpp doesn't integrate them
No unified interface for all brain subsystems

issues.title: Memory System Integration Gaps
issues.description: Memory systems declared in Brain but not properly integrated or initialized
examples: Brain.hpp includes NeuralWorkingMemory, NeuralEpisodicMemory, NeuralAssociativeMemory getters
These systems have implementations but Brain.cpp doesn't initialize them
No integration between memory systems and brain's learning mechanisms

issues.title: Prediction System Integration Issues
issues.description: Prediction systems exist but are not integrated with brain's core functionality
examples: Brain.hpp includes PredictionSystem and NeuralPrediction getter
Main.cpp doesn't use prediction system
No error signal propagation to neuromodulatory systems

issues.title: Configuration Integration Issues
issues.description: Config system is partially implemented but not fully integrated
examples: Config.hpp has sophisticated design but Config.cpp missing implementations
main.cpp uses Config but many settings are hardcoded
No configuration options for memory or prediction system parameters

issues.title: Tight Coupling and Single Responsibility Violations
issues.description: Brain class handles too many responsibilities and is tightly coupled to all subsystems
examples: Brain manages neural regions, spike systems, plasticity, memory, prediction, cognition, neuromodulation
Direct dependencies on all subsystem headers in Brain.cpp
No abstraction layer for different brain subsystems

issues.title: Inconsistent Implementation Patterns
issues.description: Different implementation patterns across systems cause maintenance issues
examples: Some plasticity rules have real implementations, others are stubs
Memory systems use different patterns (old Memory.hpp vs new NeuralWorkingMemory.cpp)
No consistent architecture for system integration

issues.title: Test Coverage for New Systems
issues.description: Tests exist for core neural computation but missing for newer systems
examples: test_stdp.cpp, test_brain.cpp, test_neuron.cpp exist and are comprehensive
No tests for neural memory systems
No tests for prediction systems
No tests for cognitive or neuromodulatory systems

issues.title: Documentation Inconsistencies
examples: Memory.hpp line 10: 'TODO - Phase 2 will implement real working memory'
PredictionSystem.hpp line 10: 'TODO - Phase 2 will implement real predictive coding'
PlasticityRule.hpp line 9: 'PLACEHOLDER - Phase 2 will implement real plasticity rules'

issues.title: Complex Configuration
issues.description: Configuration is complex and partially implemented
examples: Config.hpp has sophisticated design with variant types
Config.cpp missing loadFromFile() and loadFromArgs() implementations
Hardcoded values in main.cpp instead of config-driven approach

issues.title: Limited High-Level APIs
issues.description: No high-level APIs for common use cases
examples: Direct Brain manipulation required for most operations
No simplified interfaces for learning or prediction tasks
Complex initialization required for each use case

high: Implement Config.cpp with proper file loading and type conversion
Complete Brain.cpp integration of all memory and prediction systems
Implement missing cognitive and neuromodulatory systems
medium: Add comprehensive test coverage for neural memory and prediction systems
Implement high-level APIs for common use cases
Add configuration options for memory and prediction systems
low: Refactor Brain class to reduce interface surface area
Add utility functions for system integration

implementation_roadmap.phase_2: Implement Missing Cognitive and Neuromodulatory Systems
